name: Jacob Frey
summary: Minneapolis mayor and former city council member who backed a higher municipal minimum wage, championed zoning changes to expand housing supply, and opposed rent caps. He retained the police department while pursuing reforms, signed a climate equity plan, and issued executive orders protecting access to lawful reproductive and gender-affirming care.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Frey launched a police recruitment campaign in 2024 and negotiated a new contract with the police union. His administration retained the department while implementing reforms.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Frey increased funding for the Affordable Housing Trust Fund and started the 4d incentive, both of which support the continued supply of rental homes.

abortion-legal.rationale: After Roe was overturned, Frey ordered city agencies to decline requests from other states to investigate or detain people for providing or obtaining reproductive care that was legal in Minnesota, subject to binding legal requirements.

build-apartments-freely.rationale: Frey championed the adopted Minneapolis 2040 plan, which allows up to three dwellings on lots formerly reserved for single-family homes and directs larger apartment buildings to suitable sites.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Frey championed the Minneapolis 2040 zoning overhaul. His office reported to HUD that the city reshaped zoning maps to address the residential segregation left by earlier discriminatory policies and expand housing options in historically exclusionary neighborhoods.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Frey signed the Climate Equity Plan, which set goals to cut climate pollution substantially by 2030 and make Minneapolis carbon neutral by 2050.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In his January 2024 veto letter, Frey explicitly supported a two-state solution with a sovereign Israel and a sovereign Palestine.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Has consistently supported cannabis legalization and ordered psychedelic plant enforcement to be lowest priority; no stated view on other drugs.

limit-guns.rationale: Frey signed an ordinance banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines. The city’s announcement noted that state preemption limits its ability to enforce those restrictions.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: Frey signed an ordinance requiring owners of covered commercial and multifamily buildings to report energy performance data annually to the city for public disclosure.

open-government-data.rationale: Frey launched a public dashboard that ties city work to measurable goals and publishes progress data on priorities including public safety, climate action and homelessness.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: Frey ordered city personnel to protect access to lawful gender-affirming care and specifically directed them to uphold eligible minors’ right to consent to such care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Frey voted for the 2017 ordinance phasing in a $15 minimum wage and amended how it classified franchise businesses. The ordinance justified the increase by citing what local workers needed to earn to cover basic expenses.

rent-control.rationale: In his written response on rent stabilization, Frey argued that rent caps fail to contain rents and worsen housing shortages. He called for more market-rate and deeply affordable housing instead.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Frey’s platform called for funding programs with demonstrated results and ending those that fail to deliver, even when doing so takes political courage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Frey co-founded the Big Gay Race to help defeat a Minnesota constitutional amendment that would have restricted marriage to opposite-sex couples. The race raised more than $250,000 for that effort.

notes: This pass reviewed the council record, executive orders, budget and campaign materials, interviews, and the local transcript and Gutenberg indexes. Economy and housing searches covered wages, bargaining, worker ownership, housing supply and rent caps. Government, liberty, society and culture searches covered police, elections and mayoral powers, public records, racial equity, language access, marriage, reproductive care and transgender rights. World, globalism and means searches covered Israel and Palestine, Ukraine, trade, immigration enforcement and protest. Ecology and technology searches covered municipal emissions, environmental reporting and data centers. Positions on national immigration levels remain undocumented in the sources reviewed; Frey’s restrictions on city cooperation with immigration enforcement concern how existing laws are enforced.
